candidates.semantics: preserve the fully-mixed prefix modality sequence exactly, fill each modality slot with the highest training-only mechanics-quality envelopes available for that modality, then retain incumbent relative order for the remaining envelopes
move the first available Ukrainian envelopes into the fixed prefix, then retain incumbent relative order
candidates.hypothesis: the incumbent byte tokenizer costs about 1.868 tokens per Ukrainian codepoint on current controlled evidence, so an early Ukrainian prefix may help the byte-expensive modality before returning to the same mixed token multiset

quality_proxy.confound_control: quality-first preserves the fully-mixed prefix source sequence exactly so quality ordering is not a hidden modality curriculum

decision_rule.primary_metric: paired final aggregate heldout BPB delta versus fully_mixed

truth_boundary: Same model architecture, InitSpec family, tokenizer, optimizer recipe, precision, total optimized-token budget and incumbent MixturePlan trace multiset are used for every candidate.
Candidate schedules are deterministic permutations of the incumbent source/offset envelopes, not a second source scheduler.
Quality-first preserves the fully-mixed prefix modality sequence and reorders envelopes only within modality, isolating quality ordering from the separate Ukrainian-first modality hypothesis.
Final modality token counts and exact training batch multiset must be identical across candidates.
The current multilingual fixture is tiny, project-authored and recycled; results are mechanics evidence, not representative-corpus evidence.
No held-out probe may influence candidate construction, quality scoring or the predeclared decision rule.
